title: Tree-path and support-chain derived hulls agree
statement: Let Λ be any condensed commutative ring and X a qcqs scheme. The hull supportedModelHull Λ X defined using finite support chains [def-sfb-supported-model-hull] equals supportedImageGenerationHull Λ X defined using paths in finite qcqs open-closed trees [lem-sfb-supported-image-bounded-derived-generation, def-sfb-qcqs-open-closed-tree]. Their admissibility predicates agree as well. The extension functors are actual composites and are compared by natural isomorphisms; no replacement of any support map occurs.

proof.text: Induct on a tree path to obtain its chain. The complement at a closed edge is compact because the open subtree has compact source and its continuous image is exactly that complement. Whiskering the inductive natural isomorphism compares the actual extension functors.

proof.text: Induct on a finite chain from a qcqs root. An open edge has a reduced closed complement; a closed edge has its canonical open complement, compact by the chain hypothesis. Quasi-compact immersions preserve compactness of sources over a compact target and preserve quasi-separatedness. Add a leaf on the complementary side at each edge. This gives a tree path with the same composite extension functor.
